points.why: It names the limits-to-growth pattern and identifies the number of potential customers in the niche as the binding constraint.
It says extra spend bought nothing and raised cost per customer because the market constraint pushes back, and frames the plateau as success, not breakage.
It recommends expanding into adjacent segments, new products and new geographies, and resetting forecasts to plan around saturation.

pitfalls.why: It mentions ruling out a broken funnel only as a brief verification step; it does not go hunting for one.
It explicitly advises against doubling spend and recommends cutting it back.
